title: In vitro-Digested Cervus nippon Velvet Antler Polypeptides Alleviate Alcoholic Liver Disease by Suppressing CYP2E1 Activity and Enhancing AMPK Signaling Pathway.
authors: Hao, Zezhuang; Wang, Yihua; Yang, Haohan; Zhang, Ce; Li, Yong; Wang, Ye; Yan, Yuli; Huang, Xiaowei; Ding, Yuling
one_liner_zh: 该文研究鹿茸多肽对酒精性肝病的保护作用，涉及CYP2E1分子对接，但核心是肝脏疾病机制与功能食品，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Deer antler velvet (DAV), historically documented in Shennong's Classic of Materia Medica, is traditionally valued as a functional food believed to promote liver and kidney health and to strengthen the musculoskeletal system. Modern research highlights the bioactivity of sika deer (Cervus nippon Temminck) velvet antler peptides (sVAP), though their potential against alcoholic liver disease (ALD) remains unclear. This study aims to prepare sVAP through in vitro digestion and systematically evaluate their potential protective effects against ALD, while further elucidating the underlying mechanisms of action. Our findings demonstrate that the 1-3 kDa fraction (sVAP-1-3 kDa) exhibited the strongest hepatoprotection, reducing alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), triglyceride (TG), total cholesterol (TC), and malondialdehyde (MDA) while enhancing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione (GSH). It alleviated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, suppressed apoptosis and lipid deposition, and activated nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) signaling. Network pharmacology predicted 430 targets enriched in cytochrome P450 metabolism, lipid regulation, and inflammation. Docking showed strong binding of CYP2E1 to peptide motifs such as DFGFDGD, YFPH, FPAVP, and TYFPH. Western blotting confirmed that sVAP-1-3 kDa modulated CYP2E1/Nrf2/HO-1 and AMPK pathways, downregulating CYP2E1, SREBP-1c, FAS and PPARgamma while upregulating Nrf2, HO-1, p-AMPKalpha. This study employed simulated in vitro digestion to prepare sVAP first. sVAP-1-3 kDa exerts antioxidative and anti-lipogenic effects, thereby attenuating oxidative stress, lipid synthesis, and ALD progression, providing pharmacological evidence for the traditional use of DAV. PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS: Polypeptides extracted from antler velvet, a substance with both medicinal and dietary value, have been shown to exert therapeutic effects against alcoholic liver disease and may serve as promising candidates for the development of functional foods beneficial to individuals with excessive alcohol consumption.
abstract_zh: 鹿茸（DAV），历史上记载于《神农本草经》，传统上被视为一种功能性食品，被认为能促进肝肾健康并增强肌肉骨骼系统。现代研究强调了梅花鹿（Cervus nippon Temminck）鹿茸肽（sVAP）的生物活性，但其对酒精性肝病（ALD）的潜在作用仍不明确。本研究旨在通过体外消化制备sVAP，并系统评估其对ALD的潜在保护作用，同时进一步阐明其作用机制。我们的研究结果表明，1-3 kDa组分（sVAP-1-3 kDa）表现出最强的肝脏保护作用，降低了丙氨酸氨基转移酶（ALT）、天冬氨酸氨基转移酶（AST）、甘油三酯（TG）、总胆固醇（TC）和丙二醛（MDA）水平，同时增强了超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）和谷胱甘肽（GSH）水平。它减轻了活性氧（ROS）积累，抑制了细胞凋亡和脂质沉积，并激活了核因子E2相关因子2（Nrf2）信号通路。网络药理学预测了430个靶点，富集于细胞色素P450代谢、脂质调节和炎症通路。分子对接显示CYP2E1与肽基序如DFGFDGD、YFPH、FPAVP和TYFPH有强结合。Western blotting证实sVAP-1-3 kDa调节了CYP2E1/Nrf2/HO-1和AMPK通路，下调CYP2E1、SREBP-1c、FAS和PPARγ，同时上调Nrf2、HO-1、p-AMPKα。本研究首先采用模拟体外消化制备sVAP。sVAP-1-3 kDa发挥抗氧化和抗脂质生成作用，从而减轻氧化应激、脂质合成和ALD进展，为DAV的传统使用提供了药理学证据。实际应用：从鹿茸中提取的多肽，作为一种兼具药用和食用价值的物质，已被证明对酒精性肝病具有治疗作用，并可能成为开发有益于过量饮酒人群的功能性食品的有前景候选物。
